name: Clown
summary: The source frames the clown as a performer whose comic failures expose shared vulnerability and the masks of daily life.
description: The source frames the clown as a performer whose comic failures expose shared vulnerability and the masks of daily life.
characteristics: Mime can carry criticism without words
The mask exposes ordinary social masks
context: The author points to Charlie Chaplin’s wordless performance as a way comedy can show the awkwardness of modern life. In this account the clown also carries sorrow: laughter and failure make private feelings visible. This is the author’s reading of a flexible performance tradition.

name: Jester
summary: The source frames the jester as a verbal performer who uses wit to challenge powerful people from within their circle.
description: The source frames the jester as a verbal performer who uses wit to challenge powerful people from within their circle.
characteristics: Words and timing do the work
The performer remains dependent on the court
context: The article places the jester in the setting of medieval courts and describes a performer who could entertain while speaking uncomfortable truths. It also stresses a tension: a jester’s access and livelihood depended on the same power being criticized. The court setting is a historical frame in the source, not a claim that all jesters held the same freedom.

name: Fool
summary: The source describes the fool as an outsider who can unsettle accepted rules through paradox, play, and difficult truths.
description: The source describes the fool as an outsider who can unsettle accepted rules through paradox, play, and difficult truths.
characteristics: The outsider role permits sharp questions
context: The author uses the wise or sacred fool to discuss rule breaking and change. Religious figures and traditions appear as the author’s analogies, not as a universal classification of those figures. In this framework, the fool’s apparently unserious position can make a serious challenge easier to hear.

name: Trickster
summary: The source presents the trickster as an ambiguous agent of mischief and change whose actions can help and harm.
description: The source presents the trickster as an ambiguous agent of mischief and change whose actions can help and harm.
characteristics: Stories differ by culture and teller
context: The article names Coyote and Raven among examples from different storytelling traditions. It treats transformation as central, but its broad comparisons should not erase the distinct origins and meanings of those stories. The related Trickster profiles below give more specific cultural context and their own sources.
